Subject: Request for medical leave and temporary accommodations

Hi Laura,

I wanted to let you know that my physician has recommended a medical leave starting the week of Feb 1 for approximately 6-8 weeks (subject to recovery). I've attached the doctor's note for HR.

I'd like to request an official medical leave and discuss a phased return-to-work plan when I'm ready to come back. If possible, I'd also like to explore a part-time/remote-first ramp for the first 2–4 weeks to ease back into on-call and high-focus work.

Key details:
- Estimated leave start: 2026-02-01
- Estimated return: mid-March to early April (TBD)
- Attachment: doctors_note_marissa_20260114.pdf

Can we set up a short call with HR to go over next steps and benefits paperwork? I'm copying Mina to help with the process.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks for the heads up, Marissa — and I appreciate you sharing the note. I’m sorry to hear you’re dealing with this and want to make sure we support you however we can.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick sync this week (30 min) so we can align on dates and priorities to cover while you're out.
2) HR (Mina) will kick off the leave paperwork and short-term disability paperwork if needed.
3) We'll draft a provisional return-to-work (RTW) plan and accommodations list — I can put together an initial version and share for your input.

A couple of clarifying questions for planning purposes:
- Do you expect any changes to your planned unpaid/paid leave mix (FMLA/STD/vacation)? Mina may need to confirm benefits eligibility.
- Would you prefer to list a tentative return date (even if it might change) so we can coordinate coverage for on-call rotations and ongoing projects?

Marcus — looping you in so we can decide how to redistribute on-call and the immediate sprint workload.

I'm free for a 30-min call Tue or Wed afternoon. Marissa, what works for you?

Best,
Laura Bennett

Hi all — following our catch-up and Mina's notes, I put together a draft return-to-work plan for Marissa. Attaching the version (rtw_plan_marissa_v1.docx).

Summary (draft):
- Start date: Monday, 2026-03-08 (tentative, pending final clearance from Dr. Soni).
- Weeks 1–2 (Mar 8–Mar 19): remote-first, 60% time (3 days full, 2 half-days) focusing on low-context tasks; no on-call duties.
- Weeks 3–4 (Mar 22–Apr 2): transition to 80% time (4 days in full), limited on-call (shadow only); avoid overnight pager rotations for first 4 weeks.
- Weeks 5–6 (Apr 5–Apr 16): full duties resume, reintroduce on-call with gradual escalation.
- Accommodations: ergonomic chair, adjustable schedule (start between 9–11am), protected focus blocks (no meetings Mon/Wed 10–12) for first 3 weeks.
- Manager checkpoints: weekly 30-min sync (Laura + Marissa) for first 6 weeks; HR check-in at week 3 (Mina).
- Success criteria: returning to full schedule without symptoms impacting reliability; physician clearance required to end phased plan early.

I've also summarized required operational actions: update on-call rotation, reassign two active tickets owned by Marissa for the leave window, and patch handover notes in the team repo. Marcus, can you confirm coverage for the on-call gap and ticket redirects?

Forwarded for quick reference: excerpt from Dr. Soni's note (received directly from Marissa's physician):

> From: Dr. Soni <dr.soni@occ-health.org>
> Date: Tue, 14 Jan 2026 16:05:00 -0500
> Subject: Medical clearance note for M. Cole
> 
> Patient may require an initial phased return to work following surgery. Recommend limited hours for first 2 weeks and avoidance of overnight shift work for 4 weeks. Clearance to return pending follow-up exam in early March.

Let me know if there are edits — Marissa, feel free to mark anything you'd like adjusted. If this looks good, Mina can finalize benefits paperwork and I can lock the schedule in with the team calendar.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
